title: Efficient ATE Estimation with a Nondifferentially Misreported Binary Exposure and Internal Validation
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; math referee PASS with all cited leaves verified.
gap_reasons: Leading-journal significance remains limited by the specialized binary-report experiment with scalar covariates and fixed validation probability, without resolving a broader measurement-error problem.

Novelty positioning remains unsubstantiated: the note expressly leaves the especially close Robins--Hsieh--Newey (1995) and Xu--Kim--Li (2017) theorem scopes unaudited, and it omits a theorem-level comparison to the related two-phase outcome/covariate-error efficiency literature; audit these sources and state precisely why their model, canonical bound, and attainable estimator do or do not cover this restricted continuum result.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed the continuum canonical reduction, strict-gain/equality frontier, finite C2 pilot and conditional-solver construction, studentization, and local squared-risk attainment; the math referee passed all claims and verified every cited leaf. Updated implementation dependencies required refreshing the affected proof component and resolving its question through the reviewed VC workflow; independent audit confirmed expected stale-proof invalidation, so no pipeline code was changed. D0.5 assessed incremental tier with ceiling 6.3 below the field floor 7.4, while closest-prior theorem audits remain incomplete; the run stopped before F and has no Lean verification or substrate promotion.
tldr: Internal validation identifies the causal ATE with an error-prone binary exposure report. Under nondifferential reporting, the full continuum canonical gradient is evaluated by a pointwise two-by-two outcome-score solve and an integrated two-by-two channel solve. An observable report contrast gives the exact equality criterion and strict gain throughout the accepted informative-channel class. Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-implementation} proves the concrete finite original-record procedure from the primitive \(C^2\) bounds, with normalized-density fourth moments, coefficient-dependent midpoint integration, and uniform scaled second-moment remainder control. Theorem~\ref{thm:primitive-attainment} proves its unconditional restricted-class normal limit, consistent studentization, local regularity, and compact uniform local squared-risk attainment. The unrestricted MAR gradient is a common-law comparator from a larger model; restricted achievability and sharpness apply only to the stated subclass.
gap: Barnatchez et al. establish the unrestricted validation benchmark, and Qiu et al. explain the restricted information correction. Inspected sources do not evaluate and attain that correction for the unknown continuous outcome densities and unknown nondifferential binary channel in this original-record experiment.
fill: The evaluated conditional matrices, observable equality frontier, analytic continuum certificates, normalization-aware drift, and primitive-smoothness implementation form one efficiency result. Generic projection, coarsening, and cross-fitting principles receive full credit.
